examples.title: Factorial — recursion
examples.description: Recursive 4! = 24. Watch the call stack grow to five frames (main plus four calls) and unwind again, multiplying results on the way back — the clearest way to see how the JVM resumes a method exactly where it left off.

examples.title: Fibonacci — branching recursion
examples.tagline: Every call splits in two: fib(7) = 13.
examples.description: Naive fib(7) = 13. Every call branches into two more, so the stack grows and unwinds dozens of times. A vivid look at the cost of naive recursion: the same subproblems are recomputed from scratch again and again.

examples.title: Sum of products — nested for loops
examples.tagline: Flat stack, long run: Σ i·j over a 6×6 grid.
examples.description: Sum of i*j over a 6x6 grid. A flat call stack but hundreds of steps: it showcases iinc (incrementing a counter in place, without touching the operand stack), the if_icmpgt condition and the backward goto.

examples.title: GCD — while loop and remainder
examples.description: Euclid's algorithm for (1071, 462) = 21. A loop driven by a condition rather than a counter: instead of iinc there is ifne on the remainder (irem), plus values being copied between local variable slots.
